A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRIME study, despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V1 reports original CMV and LaMP evaluations, memory-instantiation experiments, training-free personalization analyses, and user-profile replacement results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds component comparisons and qualitative examples, including EM-included PRIME results in Table A3.

M1.justification: V1 Section 5.1 describes PRIME retrieving recent user interactions at inference. V3 Section 6 and Table A3 explicitly drop episodic memory from final PRIME, distinguishing it from EM-included PRIME. This substantially changes the reported inference components, although the personalized-thinking self-distillation procedure remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CMV coverage of 133 queries from 41 users and the same LaMP-1 through LaMP-5 tasks. Added LaMP examples illustrate existing tasks; they introduce no new dataset, population, or test scenario.

E2.justification: V3 Table A3 expands the main CMV comparison with explicit retrieval-based EM across all six backbones and a separate EM-included PRIME variant. Retrieval-based EM already appeared in v1's smaller Table A2 study. The non-personalized, R1-distilled, and OPPU comparator families remain.

E3.justification: V1 generally specifies three history interactions and up to three LoRA epochs. V3 specifies four interactions and two epochs for LaMP, and up to ten epochs for NTP. These revise reported settings without establishing that experiments were rerun. Dataset splits, metrics, and backbone coverage remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds a direct PRIME versus EM-included PRIME ablation across six backbones, extending the existing memory-component analyses. It also adds LaMP-1/2 qualitative cases and the complete candidate analysis for the existing CMV case. The original profile-replacement and training-free sensitivity studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report CMV results averaged over ten runs and ten-run dataset filtering. Neither introduces seed specifications, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-reporting practice; the retained plots are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces EM entries: Llama-3.1-8B Avg changes from 31.43 to 26.88, the latter already reported for Recent in v1 Table A2. V3 adds EM-included PRIME results, including Llama-3.1-8B Avg 32.79 versus final PRIME's 34.13. PRIME's retained scores and all Table 4 scores are unchanged; these revisions do not demonstrate same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V3 simplifies the memory-update notation and explicitly writes summary-prefix and proxy-model mappings already described in v1. These are explanatory formalizations, without new mathematical assumptions, theoretical results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about cognitive dual-memory personalization, personalized thinking, the CMV benchmark, and user-history fidelity. The headline dual-memory claim remains despite v3's qualification that final PRIME omits episodic recall.

C2.justification: V3 draws the practical conclusion that episodic memory should be omitted from final PRIME because it degrades performance. It also softens the assertion that OPPU's cross-user training 'clearly violates' privacy to 'could violate' privacy. The existing limitations and profile-replacement interpretations otherwise remain.

D1.justification: V3 discloses one-epoch thought training, more explicit proxy-generation instructions, a 500-step preference-tuning budget, and pairing with up to ten negatives. Figure A11 and Table A5 supply LaMP prompts and task substitutions. The previous 512-token limit for non-thinking variants is no longer documented; hardware and project-access information remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds Tsai et al. (2024) and contrasts its larger-teacher reasoning distillation with PRIME's self-distillation. It removes the previous model-scale contrast with Zhang et al. (2025a), while retaining the distinction between virtual-token and explicit-text reasoning. The broader related-work positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 revises the title, reorganizes Section 5 to distinguish DUAL from PRIME, adds thought-generation and training labels, and refines experimental descriptions and cross-references. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves earlier, Table A3 gains comparison blocks, and new appendix panels present LaMP prompts, examples, and the complete CMV analysis. V1 Figures A11–A12 are retained as v3 Figures A12–A13. Existing diagrams and plots retain their design and content.

improvement.justification: V3 improves transparency through the explicit EM-inclusion ablation, clearer comparator reporting, and additional training and LaMP-prompt details. These make the retained findings easier to assess and reproduce. The gain is limited because the abstract, conclusion, and framework illustration still emphasize dual-memory PRIME without fully reconciling that framing with the final implementation's omission of episodic recall.
